summary:
Observed on 2026-10-22 on organization Project 3. The guarded Status writer snapshots the protected enrolled cohort (then 69 memberships, 17 fields and 8 views) and refuses before any write when the observed board differs.

Cause 1, platform automation. Project 3 auto-adds new sub-issues of member issues. Root's public note on each auto-added issue (FS.GG.Governance#464 comment 6336976050; likewise #465 and FS.GG.SDD#1119) states that unenrolled extra memberships break the guarded Status writer and the sealed caller read, and that root removed the card. Enrollment remains a separate protected step. Unpublished session observation, not public evidence: the three cards took the board to 72 items, and the writer refused with transitions [] (nothing sent) until the cards were removed. Per the work-board lifecycle contract, sub-issue links are decomposition, not enrollment.

Cause 2, transient provider answers. During a GitHub incident (from 15:28Z), GraphQL intermittently answered Project 3 items with totalCount 0 and no nodes, under HTTP 200 with no errors. The two-read stability check then refused generically. One post-write readback was lost and was recovered by an independent read-only comparison. FS-GG/FS.GG.Coordination#1049 asks for the refusal reason to be kept, and for a sudden drop to 0 with an unchanged schema to be classified as transient. PR #4812 now keeps a typed private failure record for a refused migration-prepare in BoardV2Application.fs.

Lessons:
1. Expect membership drift from platform automation. Check the actual count before a guarded write, and treat a mismatch as a scope question, not a writer defect.
2. A cohort size hard-coded in a caller expires as soon as enrollment changes. Pass the expected membership to each run as an explicit, reviewed input. fdev reports that its session caller now takes a parameterized expected-item count. That caller is not delivered source, and no public evidence of it is cited here.
3. An empty-items answer is not evidence of an empty board. Wait for stable repeated reads before any write. Writes stay single-use.
4. Write In progress at dispatch, as the Status lifecycle requires, so the board shows active work (progress report 2026-10-22 16:22Z).

Limits: the counts are dated, and the current cohort is a live fact. This grants no enrollment or Status write.
title: Fixed-cohort board writers refuse when Project 3 auto-adds sub-issues or GitHub returns empty items
